correctness.rationale: Independent derivation: ≥3 white vertices in a part are permanent; four whites force exactly when both two-white sets have nonempty and distinct deleted-index signatures. Six cases partition into two punctured Cartesian rook graphs; direct symmetric-difference adjacency gives only boundary-matching bridges. Counts, regularity and exact diameters follow from degrees and shortest paths. The standalone exhaustive forcing/reconfiguration program corroborates all 36 pairs (3≤a,b≤8); finite checking is not proof for all pairs.

value.rationale: The exact feasible-set count was known, but local exchanges among optimum sets are not encoded in that count. The graph-isomorphism theorem establishes continuous feasible reconfiguration, uniform local flexibility, a computable adjacency model, and a sharp 3-to-4 diameter boundary for a natural first perturbation of complete bipartite graphs. The result is an infinite-family structural statement, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
